haiku-low.q1: They see 'If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link.' Nothing is written and no email is sent.
haiku-low.q2: The 60-minute count is already 3 or more, so the transaction rolls back. Nothing is written or sent, and the same generic message appears.
haiku-low.q3: 30 minutes from creation (expires_at). A newer link request or a successful reset sets used_at, which ends it sooner.
haiku-low.q4: Nothing is written, so used_at stays NULL. The link keeps working until expires_at, so the user can resubmit a compliant password.
haiku-low.q5: None. The reset deletes every sessions row for the user, including the current device. The user logs in at /login with the new password.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries up to 3 times with backoff, then logs the error and drops the job. The user is not told and must request a new reset.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token exists in API memory, the queued job, the email, and the URL. The API hashes the URL token with SHA-256 and matches it to token_hash.
haiku-low.q8: It computes SHA-256 of the URL token and finds the reset_tokens row with that token_hash. It is valid only if used_at is NULL and expires_at is after now.
haiku-low.q9: It is the count of the account's reset_tokens rows with created_at in the last 60 minutes. Rows are never deleted, so old ones age out of the window.
haiku-low.q10: Inside the issuing transaction, after locking the users row and before inserting the new row, all unused links get used_at set to now.
haiku-low.q11: In one transaction: set used_at on the token, update password_hash, and delete all the user's sessions. The confirmation email is queued only after COMMIT.
haiku-low.q12: The token update is conditional on used_at IS NULL and expires_at > now. The second submission updates 0 rows, so it rolls back to the expired-link page.

sonnet.q1: They see the same 200 message as everyone: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is written and nothing is sent.
sonnet.q2: Inside the transaction the count of that user's reset_tokens rows from the last 60 min is already 3 or more, so it rolls back. Nothing is written or sent, and the user gets the same 200 message.
sonnet.q3: 30 minutes (expires_at = created_at + 30 min). It ends sooner if used_at is set: by a newer link being issued for the account, or by a successful reset. Opening the link doesn't burn it.
sonnet.q4: Unchanged and still live. Nothing is written, the form is shown again with the error, and the same link works until its expires_at.
sonnet.q5: None. All the user's sessions rows are deleted, including the device that did the reset. No session is created; the user is redirected to /login and logs in with the new password.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries with backoff up to 3 retries. If it still fails it logs an error and drops the job. The user is not told and has to request again.
sonnet.q7: The API generates the raw token in memory during the request and puts it in the email job's link (https://app/reset?token=<raw>). The worker sends that job by email. Only the SHA-256 hash is stored in Postgres.
sonnet.q8: It looks up reset_tokens by token_hash = SHA-256(raw token from the URL). The link is good only if the row exists, used_at IS NULL, and expires_at > now. Otherwise it shows the expired-link page.
sonnet.q9: There is no separate counter. It is the count of that account's reset_tokens rows with created_at in the last 60 min, both live and dead rows. Old requests drop out as their created_at passes 60 min.
sonnet.q10: All earlier unused links for the account are killed by setting used_at = now (not deleted). This happens inside the issuing transaction, after the rate-limit check passes and the raw token is generated, and just before the new row is inserted.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: the token's used_at is set, users.password_hash is updated, and the user's sessions rows are deleted. The password-changed email job is queued only after COMMIT.
sonnet.q12: Step a of the transaction is UPDATE reset_tokens SET used_at = now() WHERE id = <row> AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now(). Only one submit gets 1 row updated and goes on. The other gets 0 rows, rolls back, and sees the expired-link page.
